key_insight: LLM agents can help develop Earth system parameterizations, but retuned physical schemes remained strong, computationally cheaper alternatives to many learned closures.
engineering_relevance: Agent-generated differentiable JAX code could accelerate parameterization prototyping, provided physical constraints and simulation performance are validated.
method: Use warm-rain collision-coalescence as a test case.
Have agents synthesize literature, reimplement published schemes, and propose new closures.
Compare conventional, learned, and agent-generated parameterizations against high-fidelity superdroplet simulations.
evidence_signal: Across ten language models, iterative feedback reduced median rollout error for eight; two of 100 unattended agent-generated closures slightly beat the best retuned scheme on held-out rain-mass error.
watch_item: Unattended performance varied strongly by scheme and language model, and success on this test case does not establish readiness for full Earth system integration.
paper_title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
